question: Should OpenClaw add a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract in core/plugin APIs, document Redis/BullMQ orchestration as external-only, or defer until narrower HA/runtime trackers settle?
rationale: The current request crosses product architecture, plugin/core boundaries, config/schema, operational dependencies, and security review scope, so automation cannot pick the permanent ownership model safely.

options.title: Design backend-neutral contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad architecture tracker and define the minimal core/plugin API seam before choosing Redis/BullMQ or another backend implementation.

options.title: Document external orchestration only
options.body: Treat ScalyClaw-style Redis/BullMQ deployments as outside OpenClaw core unless a concrete missing plugin API is identified.

options.title: Defer to narrower trackers
options.body: Leave implementation decisions to cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, and worker-auth issues, then revisit this umbrella later.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad architecture tracker and define the minimal core/plugin API seam before choosing Redis/BullMQ or another backend implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already routed this issue as architecture input and is the clearest owner for deciding core versus plugin/product direction.
